gaps.sentence: The exam, the results of ___ will be published on Friday, was very difficult.
gaps.hint: quantity noun + of + thing in a non-defining clause
gaps.explanation: 'The results of which' joins the clauses formally; 'of whom' is for people and 'of them' cannot link clauses after a comma.

gaps.sentence: He passed all his exams first time, ___ surprised everyone.
gaps.hint: refers to the whole previous clause
gaps.explanation: 'Which' can refer to a whole idea ('he passed first time'); this non-defining use never takes 'that'.

gaps.sentence: Anyone ___ wants to join the trip should sign up today.
gaps.explanation: 'Anyone who' is the standard pattern; 'who' is the subject pronoun for people.

gaps.sentence: Tell me ___ you said to her.
gaps.explanation: 'What you said' means 'the words that you said'; 'that' cannot head the clause after 'me'.

gaps.sentence: The new bridge, ___ cost two billion euros, opened last month.
gaps.hint: thing + extra information after a comma
gaps.explanation: 'Which' introduces non-defining clauses about things; 'that' is forbidden there.

gaps.sentence: The woman ___ won the prize gave a short speech.
gaps.explanation: The gap is the subject pronoun for a person, so 'who' is needed; 'whose' would show possession.

gaps.sentence: My colleague Anna, ___ joined us in May, has already been promoted.
gaps.explanation: 'Who' refers to Anna; non-defining clauses never use 'that'.

gaps.sentence: The hotel, ___ rates include breakfast, is fully booked for the conference.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' marks possession even for things: the hotel whose rates…
